intuition: Enumerate every start/end pair and accumulate sums in O(n²) time. Every new endpoint shares almost all earlier candidates, suggesting that a compact summary should replace repeated subarray enumeration.

The summary is ending: the best sum of a nonempty subarray ending at the immediately previous position. To include the next value, either extend that subarray or abandon it and start fresh. A negative prefix is a burden, while a positive one improves the next choice. Keep a separate best because the globally optimal subarray may end long before the last element. Initializing with an actual element preserves the nonempty requirement on all-negative input.

Every subarray ending at i either starts at i or extends a subarray ending at i-1. Choosing the better option gives the optimal ending sum by induction. Taking the maximum over all ending positions therefore covers every nonempty subarray. Only two running sums are needed.

steps: Initialize ending=best=-2 at the first element.
At value 1, restarting beats extending -2, so ending=1 and best=1.
At value 4, restarting beats the preceding ending=-2, beginning the useful middle segment.
Extend through -1,2,1 to reach ending=6 for [4,-1,2,1].
Later values do not exceed best=6, so return that stored global optimum.

codeNotes.note: A real first element gives the correct result even when every possible subarray has a negative sum.
These are the only ways a contiguous subarray can end here: start here or extend the previous prefix optimum.
Preserve earlier optimal endpoints instead of accidentally returning only the last ending sum.
